comparisons.peer_summary: Client net revenue increased to $7.1 billion in 2024 from $4.7 billion in 2023, a 52% increase driven by a 34% rise in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose that their revenue growth in 2024 was driven by a combination of increased product shipments (volume) and higher average selling prices (ASP). However, the composition differs: Micron's 62% total revenue growth was driven by a 60% increase in DRAM sales (mid-40% bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth) and a 72% increase in NAND sales. In contrast, AMD's Client segment grew 52%, driven by a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in ASP, reflecting strong demand for Ryzen processors.

sentences.text: Total revenue for 2024 increased 62% as compared to 2023 primarily due to increases in sales of both DRAM and NAND products.
• Sales of DRAM products increased 60% primarily due to a mid-40% range increase in bit shipments and a low-teen percentage range increase in average selling prices.
• Sales of NAND products increased 72% primarily due to a low-30% range increase in bit shipments and a low-30% percentage range increase in average selling prices.

Client net revenue of $7.1 billion in 2024 increased by 52%, compared to net revenue of $4.7 billion in 2023, primarily due to a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price driven by strong demand for AMD mobile and desktop Ryzen processors.

comparisons.peer_summary: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023, driven by higher server revenue from high core count products, which increased average selling prices but lowered volume compared to 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Intel disclose that shifts in product mix toward higher-value items drove changes in Average Selling Prices (ASPs), though with opposite net revenue impacts. Micron’s DRAM sales increased 60% due to low-teen ASP growth alongside mid-40% bit shipment growth. Intel’s DCAI revenue increased only 1% because, while high core count products increased ASPs, they also led to lower volume compared to the prior year, partially offsetting the ASP benefit. Thus, Micron benefited from concurrent volume and ASP gains, whereas Intel faced volume headwinds against ASP gains.

comparisons.peer_summary: Compute & Networking revenue increased year-on-year, driven by a 266% growth in Compute due to higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for LLMs, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, as well as a 133% increase in Networking due to higher InfiniBand shipments.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies attribute significant 2024 revenue growth to specific product shipment increases. Micron reports a 60% increase in DRAM sales due to mid-40% bit shipment growth and a 72% increase in NAND sales due to low-30% bit shipment growth. Similarly, NVIDIA's Compute & Networking revenue surged, with Compute growing 266% due to higher shipments of the Hopper GPU platform and Networking increasing 133% due to higher InfiniBand shipments. While Micron's drivers are broad memory bit-volume and ASP expansions, NVIDIA's are dominated by specific AI accelerator and networking platform volumes.
